hep-ph.title: Precision Measurements of the Effective Leptonic Weak Mixing Angle at Hadron Colliders
hep-ph.author: Arie Bodek, Hyon-San Seo, Un-Ki Yang
hep-ph.abstract: We review precision determinations of the effective leptonic weak mixing angle, $\sin^2\theta^\ell_{\mathrm{eff}}$, from Drell-Yan angular asymmetries at the Tevatron and the LHC. As statistical uncertainties have dramatically decreased, parton distribution function (PDF) uncertainty now dominates the most precise hadron-collider results. We describe the angular observables, electroweak calculation schemes, and advanced methods such as replica reweighting and Hessian profiling, used to constrain PDFs directly from measured angular distributions. To identify the origin of differences between modern PDF sets (e.g., CT18, MSHT20, NNPDF) in the extracted mixing angle, we employ a simplified leading-order Z-pole calculation that separates quark-flavor production weights from quark-direction dilution. We demonstrate how these PDF-induced differences can be mitigated by incorporating complementary constraints from W/Z cross-section ratios and W-boson decay asymmetries. Furthermore, we discuss the requirements for a common reinterpretation and future combination of LHC measurements, highlighting how correlated PDF uncertainties limit the ultimate combined precision. Finally, we outline future prospects, including complementary measurements in $Z+b$ production and high-mass tests of the running $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ weak mixing angle.

hep-ph.title: Positron escape from dark matter spikes in black hole X-ray binaries
hep-ph.author: Mpho Kgoadi, Geoff Beck
hep-ph.abstract: Chan and Lee present a model where the AMS-02 positron excess is explained by dark matter (DM) annihilation in spike halos around nearby black holes A0620-00 and XTE J1118+480. Their model assumes a uniform magnetic and diffusive environment en route to Earth. Thus, it depends on the assumption that one can ignore the small-scale, near-horizon environment in the diffusion-loss equation. We demonstrate that this is not the case. An accurate magnetic field model near the horizon means, without increasing the required cross-section by a factor of roughly 500 to 1400, depending on the transport near the horizon, the positron flux from these sources cannot account for a significant fraction of the AMS-02 excess.

hep-ph.title: Radii of Sn Isotopes near the Proton Dripline from Nuclear Lattice Effective Field Theory
hep-ph.author: Fabian Hildenbrand, Serdar Elhatisari, Ulf-G. Meißner
hep-ph.abstract: We present the first $\textit{ab initio}$ lattice calculations of charge and matter radii of tin isotopes $^{96}$Sn, $^{98}$Sn, $^{100}$Sn, $^{102}$Sn and $^{104}$Sn near the proton dripline using nuclear lattice effective field theory with high-fidelity two- and three-nucleon forces combined with the partial-pinhole algorithm. The resulting radii are larger then predicted from other ab-initio methods. We find that variations of the three-nucleon interaction reveal substantial radius differences even among interactions with similar binding energies. We intensively discuss of the role of different choices of the three-body forces.

hep-ph.title: Instanton tunnelling as a verifiable benchmark for digital quantum simulation: circuit structure, classical simulability and hardware reproducibility
hep-ph.author: Gerhard Hellstern, Marc Maussner
hep-ph.abstract: We use instanton-mediated tunnelling in the quartic double well as a benchmark for digital quantum simulation that is checkable against an exact answer at every step. The instanton enters through the classical analysis; the hardware tests the dynamics of the lattice model. A unary (single-excitation) encoding maps N lattice sites to N qubits, with the single-excitation dynamics as a reference that remains classically cheap at any N. For a second-order Trotter circuit with adjacent, equal-angle XX/YY pairs on each bond, we prove that the Schmidt rank across any cut is at most four at every gate boundary and at most two after each pair, independently of N. Matrix-product-state simulations of this gate list reproduce the exact splitting up to N = 48. For this bond-wise formula the admissible Trotter step shrinks roughly as N^-2, so one tunnelling period costs about N^3.3 two-qubit gates; a kinetic/potential splitting keeps the step near 0.065 up to N=128, so this scaling belongs to splitting the kinetic term bond by bond. At a coarser, separately bounded step we measure the full transfer at N=8 on two superconducting processors, recovering the lattice splitting to a few percent and its dependence on the barrier height, which at this resolution is set by the lattice rather than by the instanton. Over 9 repetitions, runs taken minutes apart agree to shot noise, while runs hours to weeks apart differ by up to 6.1%, also on a fixed set of qubits; with sessions as the sampling unit, the processors differ in the damping, while a difference in the splitting is not established. Normalising by the measured single-excitation population extends the usable depth about 4-fold but does not improve the splitting. A Gaussian start state, which needs no diagonalisation, reproduces the splitting of the eigenvector-based start to within 1.6 percentage points.

hep-ph.title: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA stochastic constraints on first-order phase transitions: A tale of priors
hep-ph.author: S. AbdusSalam(1), J. Kersten(2, 3, 4), S. A. Ojaghi(1), L. Velasco-Sevilla(2), A. Zafari(1) ((1) Department of Physics, Shahid Beheshti University, (2) Department of Physics and IPAP, Yonsei University, (3) Department of Physics and Technology, University of Bergen, (4) School of Physics, Korea Institute for Advanced Study)
hep-ph.abstract: We re-examine the methodology for constraining cosmological first-order phase transitions from gravitational-wave searches using Bayesian statistical analysis. Specifically, we use results from LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA searches for a stochastic gravitational wave background during observing runs O1--O4a. We explore multiple prior choices across three categories of fit parameters: geometrical parameters, thermodynamical parameters of phase transitions, and the parameters of an Abelian Higgs particle physics model. Our key finding is that the constraints on most parameters describing gravitational waves from a phase transition depend strongly on the prior. Consequently, the data do not yet allow to derive robust constraints on these parameters. Besides, even if a parameter is meaningfully constrained, the upper limit can vary significantly with the prior range. We provide practical recommendations for assessing the robustness of parameter estimates and guidelines for rigorously testing prior independence in future analyses.

hep-ph.title: Light fermions can trigger a Brout-Englert-Higgs effect
hep-ph.author: Axel Maas, Sofie Martins, Georg Wieland
hep-ph.abstract: The Brout-Englert-Higgs effect produces the masses of the Standard Model particles. However, the cause of this effect is unknown. Beyond-the-Standard-Model theories aim to find the source of this effect, for example using a composite Higgs and dynamically generating its vacuum expectation value. In this paper, we show evidence from lattice simulations with vectorially coupled fermions and without Yukawa couplings that the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect could be triggered by the light masses of fermions. This suggests that an explanation entirely within the Standard Model could be possible. Moreover, our results are consistent with weak couplings and fermions can only impact the Higgs potential at NNLO. This implies a so far unidentified mechanism in an SU(2) scalar-fermion-gauge system that produces a non-zero vacuum expectation value. In addition, we find that the transition from a QCD-like behavior to a Higgs-like behavior happens when the fermion mass falls below twice the W/Z mass: a threshold that is integer valued but not connected to other critical physical behavior.

hep-ph.title: Three-nucleon potentials and their matrix elements for $δ_{\mathrm{NS}}$ in superallowed $β$ decays
hep-ph.author: Graham Chambers-Wall, Maria Dawid, Emanuele Mereghetti, Saori Pastore, Maria Piarulli
hep-ph.abstract: We derive three-nucleon potentials for radiative corrections at order $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_\chi^2)$ in chiral effective field theory where $\alpha$ is the electromagnetic coupling and $\epsilon_\chi$ is the chiral expansion parameter. These corrections contribute to the nuclear-structure-dependent term $\delta_\mathrm{NS}$ for determinations of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix element $V_{ud}$ from superallowed nuclear $\beta$ decays. We compute matrix elements of three-nucleon contributions at orders $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ and $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_\chi^2)$ using quantum Monte Carlo methods. We find the matrix elements at order $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ to be large and to have an effect on the extraction of $V_{ud}$ at the scale of $10^{-4}$. In the case of $^{10}$C, the matrix elements of $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_\chi^2)$ three-nucleon operators provide a 2% correction to $\delta_{\text{NS}}$, and are thus beyond the current precision goals. The relative size of three-nucleon corrections to $\delta_{\text{NS}}$ in medium mass nuclei, where two-body contributions tend to be smaller, remains to be investigated. We then use these results to determine $V_{ud}$ from the superallowed transition ${}^{10}\mathrm{C}\rightarrow{}^{10}\mathrm{B}$.

hep-ph.title: From geometric curvature to effective backgrounds: a dictionary for Dirac fermions in one, two and three spatial dimensions
hep-ph.author: David Valenzuela, Alfredo Raya
hep-ph.abstract: Dirac equation on curved backgrounds can be rewritten as a flat-space equation in which geometry appears as a tensorial Fermi velocity together with a set of background fields. We derive this correspondence from a single Clifford-algebra identity and follow it through one, two, and three spatial dimensions. Once the spin connection is written in terms of Ricci rotation coefficients, only two contractions can occur. The trace produces a term with the index structure of a vector potential in every dimensionality; it enters with an imaginary factor i and is precisely the term that keeps the operator Hermitian when the Fermi velocity depends on position. The totally antisymmetric contraction produces an object that depends on the number of indices available to the Levi-Civita symbol: a trace on a line, a pseudoscalar mass on a surface, and an axial vector potential in a volume. Neither contraction is invariant under local rotations of the frame, and we give the transformation laws. On a surface, the curl of the trace term can always be removed by a frame rotation, while its divergence is proportional to the Gaussian curvature. We apply the correspondence to a Gaussian bump, where the local density of states at the center falls below its flat value and obeys a closed form at low energy; to a wire, where a nonuniform lapse binds states inside the gap and a nonuniform velocity cannot; to stationary frames on a surface, where a circulating drag shifts the Dirac mass locally with either sign; and to twisted and rotating frames in a volume, where the axial term takes the form of a chiral chemical potential produced by the frame alone, or separates Weyl nodes in a rotating sample. We separate the geometric contribution from the lattice pseudogauge field that dominates the response of strained samples

hep-ph.title: Dimension-8 SMEFT Matching Conditions for the Low-Energy Effective Field Theory
hep-ph.author: Serge Hamoudou, Jacky Kumar, David London
hep-ph.abstract: In particle physics, the modern view is to categorize things in terms of effective field theories (EFTs). Above the weak scale, we have the SMEFT, formed when the heavy new physics (NP) is integrated out, and for which the Standard Model (SM) is the leading part. Below $M_W$, we have the LEFT (low-energy EFT), formed when the heavy SM particles ($W^\pm$, $Z^0$, $H$, $t$) are also integrated out. In order to determine how low-energy measurements depend on the underlying NP, it is necessary to compute the matching conditions of LEFT operators to SMEFT operators. These matching conditions have been worked out for all LEFT operators up to dimension 6 in terms of SMEFT operators up to dimension 6 at the one-loop level. However, this is not sufficient for all low-energy observables. In this paper we present the momentum-independent matching conditions of all such LEFT operators to SMEFT operators up to dimension 8 at tree level.

hep-ph.title: Atomic Dark Matter, Interacting Dark Radiation, and the Hubble Tension
hep-ph.author: Manuel A. Buen-Abad, Zackaria Chacko, Ina Flood, Can Kilic, Gustavo Marques-Tavares, Taewook Youn
hep-ph.abstract: We present a new class of interacting dark sector models that can address the Hubble tension. Interacting dark radiation (DR) has previously been put forward as a solution to the problem, but this proposal is disfavored by the high-$\ell$ cosmic microwave background (CMB) data. We modify this basic framework by introducing a subcomponent of dark matter (DM) that interacts strongly with the DR, so that together they constitute a tightly coupled fluid at early times. We show that if this subcomponent decouples from the interacting DR during the CMB epoch, the $\ell$ modes of the CMB that entered the horizon before decoupling are impacted differently from those that entered after, allowing a solution to the problem. We present a model that realizes this framework, which we dub "New Atomic Dark Matter", or nuADaM, in which the interacting dark matter (iDM) subcomponent is composed of dark atoms, and dark "neutrinos" with long-range interactions contribute to the DR, hence the name of the model. This iDM subcomponent is acoustic at early times but decouples from the DR following dark recombination. In contrast to conventional atomic dark matter (ADM) models, the dark photon is part of a richer DR sector, which ensures that it continues to be self-interacting even after recombination. We show that this model admits a significantly larger value of $H_0$ than $\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}$ when fit to CMB and BAO data, while maintaining a comparable goodness of fit. Once the SHOES data set is included, it provides a significantly better fit than $\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}$.

hep-ph.title: Enhancement of Weak Interactions in Phase Transitions in Condensed Matter and Early Universe
hep-ph.author: V. V. Flambaum
hep-ph.abstract: Parity-violating weak interactions produce extremely small energy differences between left- and right-handed chiral systems. We show that these microscopic effects may be amplified during collective phenomena such as phase transitions. The enhancement factor is proportional to the critical number of atoms, $N_c$, in the nucleus of the new phase. Measurement of the ratio of produced left- and right-handed chiral structures may provide a way to determine $N_c$. Experiments in which spin-chiral structures are formed in ZnCr$_2$Se$_4$ during a phase transition in crossed electric and magnetic fields indicate an effective amplification corresponding to $N_c\sim 10^9-10^{10}$. We emphasize, however, that such large values cannot be inferred from homogeneous capillary nucleation alone, since the same parameters imply a very large nucleation barrier; in real crystals heterogeneous nucleation, defects, strain, and domain-growth dynamics may be essential. We also discuss, more cautiously, whether analogous collective enhancement could operate in first-order cosmological phase transitions beyond the Standard Model. The Standard-Model electroweak transition for the observed Higgs mass is a crossover and therefore has no critical bubble nucleus.

hep-ph.title: Exploring enhanced non-resonant di-Higgs production at the HL-LHC with neural networks
hep-ph.author: Leandro Da Rold, Manuel Epele, Anibal D. Medina, Nicolás I. Mileo, Alejandro Szynkman
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate di-Higgs production in the $b\bar{b}\gamma\gamma$ final state at the LHC, focusing on scenarios where the gluon fusion process is enhanced by new colored scalars, which could be identified as squarks or leptoquarks. We consider two benchmarks characterized by the mass of the lightest colored scalar, BM$_{\mathrm{L}}$ and BM$_{\mathrm{H}}$, corresponding to 464 GeV and 621 GeV, respectively. Using Monte Carlo simulations for both the signal and the dominant backgrounds, we perform a discovery analysis with deep neural networks, exploring various architectures and input variables. Our results show that the discrimination power is maximized by employing two dedicated classifiers, one trained against QCD backgrounds and another against backgrounds involving single-Higgs processes. Furthermore, we demonstrate that including high-level features -- such as the invariant masses $m_{\gamma\gamma}$, $m_{bb}$, and $m_{hh}$, as well as the transverse momenta and angular separations of the photon and $b$-jet pairs -- significantly improves the performance compared to using only low-level features as the invariant mass and momenta of the final particles. For the latter case, we find that architectures processing photon and $b$-jet variables separately can enhance the significance for BM$_{\mathrm{H}}$. Projecting for an integrated luminosity of 3 ab$^{-1}$, we obtain a significance of 7.2 for BM$_{\mathrm{L}}$, while it drops to 3.1 for BM$_{\mathrm{H}}$. In the particular case of BM$_{\mathrm{L}}$, discovery level significance can be reached at 1.4 ab$^{-1}$. We also estimate how these results could be modified by potential systematic uncertainties.

hep-ph.title: Untangling the Integration-By-Parts Equations
hep-ph.author: Junhan W. Liu, Alexander Mitov
hep-ph.abstract: In this work, we present an algorithm which converts the Integration-by-Parts (IBP) equations into single-variable recurrence relations. We refer to this procedure as {\it diagonalization}. Diagonalized IBP equations are indispensable for reducing loop integrals with extremely high numerator powers to master integrals, and for solving IBP identities in closed analytic form. A prime example is provided by multivariate Mellin representations of loop amplitudes and cross sections. The extension of these methods to other multivariate recurrence relations is also discussed. As a by-product of our diagonalization procedure, we show how the IBP equations can be cast into an efficient, fully triangular form that is well suited for computer implementation. Several complicated topologies have been computed.

hep-ph.title: Radiative Dirac Neutrino Masses from Modular $S_3$ Symmetry in an Axion Model
hep-ph.author: Sin Kyu Kang, Ranjeet Kumar, Hiroshi Okada
hep-ph.abstract: We present a unified axion model framework that simultaneously addresses the origin of neutrino masses, leptonic flavor structure, the strong CP problem, and dark matter. The model is based on a global $U(1)_{\rm PQ}$ symmetry combined with a modular $S_3$ symmetry and is realized within a novel class of KSVZ-type axion model. Exotic colored fermions and scalars mediate radiative neutrino mass generation at the one loop-level. The PQ charge assignment forbids tree-level neutrino masses and leaves a residual $Z_3$ symmetry that ensures the Dirac nature of neutrinos. In the minimal realization, the neutrino mass matrix is of rank two, predicting one massless neutrino. Consequently, the sum of neutrino masses is constrained for both the normal and inverted hierarchies. We analyze the implications for charged lepton flavor violation and the lepton $g-2$. The axion emerging from this framework dynamically resolves the strong CP problem and accounts for the observed dark matter abundance. Notably, the predicted axion-photon coupling is within reach of upcoming experiments and consistent with existing astrophysical and cosmological bounds.

hep-ph.title: Asymmetric dark matter from leptogenesis in type-III seesaw framework with modular $S_4$ symmetry
hep-ph.author: Abhishek, V. Suryanarayana Mummidi
hep-ph.abstract: We present a unified framework for neutrino masses, baryogenesis, and dark matter based on a modular $S_4$ symmetry combined with a type-III seesaw mechanism. All Yukawa couplings, CP phases, and flavor textures originate from a single complex modulus $\tau$, whose vacuum expectation value controls both visible and dark sector dynamics. The same modular parameter fixes the neutrino mass matrix, determines the CP asymmetries driving resonant leptogenesis, and correlates the resulting baryon and dark matter abundances. A detailed numerical analysis shows that the model reproduces all neutrino oscillation data within the $3\sigma$ NuFIT~5.2 (2024) ranges for normal ordering, predicting $\delta_{\rm CP} \simeq \pm (150^\circ-180^\circ)$, $\sum m_\nu\simeq(0.06-0.08)~\mathrm{eV}$, and an effective Majorana mass $m_{\beta\beta} \simeq (0.3 - 4)\times 10^{-3}~\mathrm{eV}$, testable in next-generation neutrinoless double-beta decay experiments. The same modular Yukawas yield resonantly enhanced CP asymmetries $|\epsilon_{L,\chi}| \sim 10^{-9}-10^{-6}$ at $M_\Sigma \sim 10^{7}~\mathrm{GeV}$, successfully generating the observed baryon asymmetry $\eta_B\simeq6\times10^{-10}$ and dark relic density $\Omega_\chi h^2\simeq0.12$ without additional free parameters. The predicted correlation $\Omega_\chi/\Omega_B\simeq5.4$ fixes the dark matter mass to $m_\chi\simeq0.1-2~\mathrm{GeV}$, consistent with all current constraints. This framework therefore realizes a fully predictive baryon$-$dark matter co-genesis, where the geometry of the modular symmetry links the origin of flavor, CP violation, and the cosmic matter asymmetry.

hep-ph.title: Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at future lepton colliders
hep-ph.author: Dario Buttazzo, Gabriele Levati, Yang Ma, Fabio Maltoni, Paride Paradisi, ZeQiang Wang
hep-ph.abstract: The electric and magnetic dipole moments of the electron and of the muon provide stringent tests of the Standard Model and sensitive probes of new physics. By contrast, the corresponding dipole moments of the $\tau$ lepton remain weakly constrained. This study explores the potential of future lepton colliders, focusing on the $e^+e^-$ Future Circular Collider and a multi-TeV muon collider, to probe $\tau$ dipole moments. We consider multiple channels, including $\ell^+\ell^- \to \tau^+\tau^-$ ($\ell=e,\mu$), associated Higgs production $\mu^+\mu^- \to \tau^+\tau^- H$, radiative Higgs decays $H \to \tau^+\tau^-\gamma$, and vector-boson scattering $\ell^+\ell^- \to \ell^+\ell^-\tau^+\tau^-$ and $\mu^+\mu^- \to \bar\nu\nu\tau^+\tau^-$. Our results show that these facilities are highly complementary and can extend existing bounds by several orders of magnitude.

hep-ph.title: Low-Multiplicity Jets as Probes of GeV-Scale Light-Quark-Coupled Particles
hep-ph.author: Carlos Henrique de Lima, David McKeen, Maximilian Swiatlowski
hep-ph.abstract: We propose a search at the LHC for GeV-scale particles coupling predominantly to light quarks based on low-multiplicity jets. The search targets production in association with a hard photon and uses the feature that a light gauge-singlet can only decay into a small number of hadronic channels, yielding jets with anomalously low charged-track multiplicity and mass compared to QCD jets at the same transverse momentum. We determine the sensitivity to scalar and pseudoscalar couplings to up-quarks, and suggest a data-driven estimate that reduces the sensitivity to jet modeling uncertainties. This search extends the reach to hadronically-coupled particles into a previously inaccessible regime.

hep-ph.title: Geometric algebra as the input language of collider foundation models
hep-ph.author: E. Abasov, L. Dudko, F. Grigoryev, P. Volkov, A. Zaborenko
hep-ph.abstract: We describe a hard hadron-collider event as a single geometric object. Each reconstructed final-state object is a multivector of $\Cl(1,3)\otimes\Vflav$ that combines its four-momentum with its object-type label. The event multivector $\evMV$ is the direct sum of these per-object multivectors. Products in the algebra generate the higher grades from the measured four-momenta. The grades organise nearly every observable in current use, from invariants at grade zero to decay-plane bivectors, oriented three-volumes and the CP-odd pseudoscalar at grades two to four. The high-level invariants and the low-level four-momentum recipe of earlier analyses, and the inputs of equivariant networks, are recovered as projections onto specific grades. We give a per-grade dictionary of $32$ classical observables and an inventory of the symmetries acting on $\evMV$. A theorem extending the Cayley--Menger identity to Minkowski space shows that the higher grades give no Lorentz invariant beyond $\{p_i\!\cdot\!p_j,\,m_i^2\}$ except the CP-odd sign of the pseudoscalar. Grades two and three n evertheless describe the decay planes and decay volumes of the event compactly, as covariant objects. The representation is intended as a uniform input layer for foundation models of collider physics. As a simple example of its use, we apply it to the resonance-topology separation of $pp\!\to\!tWb$ with a small Lorentz-equivariant multivector transformer of L-GATr type. In an ablation over eight input representations of this example, the classifier improves when a fixed reference bivector encoding the beam plane, which the momenta do not contain, is added to the input.

hep-ph.title: Predicted Exotic Doubly Heavy-Strange Pentaquarks
hep-ph.author: Albert Feijoo, Eulogio Oset
hep-ph.abstract: We predict exotic doubly heavy--strange pentaquarks with minimal quark content $u\bar d sQQ'$ ($QQ'=cc,bc,bb$) within a coupled-channel unitary framework where the interaction is derived from an extension of the local hidden gauge approach to the heavy-quark sector. We obtain a robust spectrum of manifestly exotic states; two states appear in the $u\bar d scc$ sector, three in $u\bar d scb$, and two in $u\bar d sbb$. These emerge either as bound states or resonances, along with seven additional virtual states manifested as threshold cusps. The binding mechanism is dominated by off-diagonal transitions among heavy-baryon--light-meson channels, while diagonal interactions are strongly suppressed. These results extend exotic hadron spectroscopy into the doubly heavy--strange sector and provide concrete targets for future experimental searches.

hep-ph.title: Dark Matter Interpretation of the Super-Kamiokande Antineutrino Excess in $\mathrm{U}(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ model
hep-ph.author: Motoi Endo, Yushi Mura, Tenta Tsuji

hep-ph.title: Lepton $g-2$ non-universality of hadronic contributions and a sub-GeV window to New Physics
hep-ph.author: Siyuan Li, Vladimir Pascalutsa, Maxim Pospelov
hep-ph.abstract: We propose the linear combination of the anomalous magnetic moments of the muon and electron, $a_{\mu-e} \equiv a_\mu - (m_\mu/m_e)^2 a_e$, as a natural low-energy window quantity that may directly probe the current discrepancy between the data-driven and lattice-QCD evaluations of hadronic contributions. The rescaling ensures an exact cancellation of the leading short-range ($m_\ell^2$-scaling) effects, thereby improving the UV behavior. Because entire classes of contributions cancel identically --- not merely in variance --- the combination is predictable in chiral perturbation theory with no free low-energy constant, and it isolates flavor-non-universal New Physics. The hadronic-vacuum-polarization effect in $a^{\rm HVP}_{\mu-e}$, together with its uncertainty, is reduced as compared to $a^{\rm HVP}_{\mu}$ by $\sim 85\%$. This is promising for tests of New Physics with some degree of flavor non-universality, conditional on significant improvements in the measurements of $a_e$ and $\alpha$.

hep-ph.title: Transverse-momentum resummation effects on angular coefficients in Z and W boson hadroproduction
hep-ph.author: Stefano Camarda, Giancarlo Ferrera, Lorenzo Rossi, Gabriele Francesco Sala
hep-ph.abstract: We present a comprehensive analysis of the angular coefficients of $Z$ and $W$ boson production at hadron colliders in different kinematical ranges, using data from the ATLAS, LHCb, and CMS Collaborations at the LHC, including the recent CMS measurement at $\sqrt{s}=13$~TeV, as well as CDF data at the Tevatron. We provide theoretical predictions obtained by consistently combining the resummation of logarithmically enhanced QCD corrections at small transverse momentum $q_T$ up to next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy (NNLL) with the fixed-order calculation through $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_S^2)$. The fixed-order helicity cross sections entering the finite component are evaluated using the new complete analytic NLO calculation implemented in the DYTurbo program. This implementation makes it possible to obtain fast and numerically stable predictions for all the angular coefficients and to perform an extensive study of their theoretical uncertainties. We quantify the impact of transverse-momentum resummation on the angular coefficients and we estimate the associated theoretical uncertainties, including scale variations, parton distribution functions, non-perturbative effects, the treatment of the transition region and the recoil prescription used to generate the lepton angular distribution of the resummed component. Within the estimated theoretical uncertainties, resummation improves the description of several measurements, particularly for $A_2$, while its impact on $A_0$ depends more strongly on the dataset and on the theoretical choices. The Lam--Tung combination $A_0-A_2$ is essentially unaffected by resummation.

hep-ph.title: Low-lying singly heavy baryon states based on the rigorous calculation with the relativized quark model
hep-ph.author: Zhen-Yu Li, Guo-Liang Yu, Zhi-Gang Wang, Jian-Zhong Gu
hep-ph.abstract: In this work, the low-lying $\mathbf{6}_{F}$ singly heavy baryon states with positive-parity are studied in detail in the framework of the relativized quark model by using the improved calculation scheme which has nicely explained the fine structure of the low-lying negative-parity singly heavy baryons. The low-lying spectra of all the singly heavy baryon families obtained in the same framework and calculation scheme are systematically analyzed. The baryon states marked with (mass)$J^{P}$ are obtained by considering the mixing effect rigorously. It is found that the mixing effect in the singly heavy baryons depends on the flavor symmetry of the two light quarks and the baryon parity. The results show that the high-precision calculation reproduces the majority of the assigned experimental masses within the maximum deviation range of 20 MeV and the mean absolute deviation between the calculated masses and the experimental data is only 6.88 MeV. The rigorous calculation achieved by the two-step GEM enables us to analyze the detailed behavior of the various strong interaction components within the baryons with a high-precision. The large amount of data obtained in this work serves as the useful references for related experimental and theoretical researches.

hep-ph.title: Estimation of the cumulant $b_4$ and sextic self-coupling of the QCD axion at finite temperature and density
hep-ph.author: Xinguang Li, Zhao Zhang
hep-ph.abstract: The sixth-order cumulant $b_4$ of the QCD topological charge distribution and the axion's sextic self-coupling at finite temperature $T$ and baryon chemical potential $\mu$ are calculated within the two-flavor quark-meson (QM) model without and with the Polyakov-loop dynamics. The $b_4$ in the vacuum falls within the range predicted by lattice SU(3) pure-gauge simulations, and at large $T$ and/or $\mu$, it tends to a constant predicted by the dilute instanton gas approximation. Both $b_4$ and the axion's sextic self-coupling diverge at the QCD critical point and flip sign across the phase transition. The range of accuracy of the fourth- and sixth-order Taylor expansions of the free energy as a function of the $\theta$ parameter is investigated via comparison with the full potential at the mean-field level.

hep-ph.title: Soft Scale Symmetry Breaking with Laguerre Explicit Regulators
hep-ph.author: A. R. Vieira
hep-ph.abstract: In this work, we search for explicit regulators that do not spuriously break scale invariance starting from conditions established by implicit regularization. There is a family of regulator functions that obeys the conditions and leads to soft breaking terms of the dilatation current. This family of functions is shown to be related to the Laguerre polynomials. We apply this approach by revisiting quadratic divergences in the context of the naturalness problem of the Standard Model and show that the quadratic dependence of the Higgs mass on the cutoff is not required by consistency of scale-symmetry breaking and can be removed within this class of regulators. Applications of these regulators beyond 1-loop order are also considered.

hep-ph.title: Spin-dependent fermion potentials from mixed tensor couplings of massive spin-1 and spin-2 bosons
hep-ph.author: D. Khadka, V.V. Flambaum
hep-ph.abstract: Searches for weak spin-dependent forces are commonly interpreted in terms of a basis of sixteen rotationally invariant two-fermion potentials. We derive finite-range coordinate-space potentials generated by a massive spin-1 boson with vector, axial-vector, tensor, and pseudotensor couplings to Dirac fermions. In addition to the familiar vector--vector, vector--axial-vector, and axial-vector--axial-vector interactions, we obtain the mixed vector--tensor, vector--pseudotensor, axial-vector--tensor, and axial-vector--pseudotensor potentials, together with tensor--tensor, tensor--pseudotensor, and pseudotensor--pseudotensor terms. We retain the contact terms needed in atomic-scale applications and give compact expressions that include both orderings of inequivalent fermion vertices. We then extend the analysis to a massive spin-2 mediator described by a symmetric Fierz--Pauli field. Besides the conventional coupling to the conserved fermion energy--momentum tensor, we consider a symmetric axial-tensor current. Its nonconservation for massive fermions makes the longitudinal spin-2 helicities contribute to axial-tensor--axial-tensor exchange. The leading minimal spin-2 interactions are either P,T even or P odd and T evenl. Heavy-mediator contact limits and the distinction between the M-->0 massive-spin-2 limit and a genuine massless graviton are also discussed. We map the resulting interactions onto the sixteen-potential Dobrescu--Mocioiu basis and use this mapping to translate existing experimental constraints into numerical limits on spin-1 and spin-2 coupling products in the small- and large-mediator-mass regimes, together with representative limits at finite mediator masses. The derived relations between the boson-exchange coupling constants and the coefficients of the basis potentials also allow published exclusion curves to be rescaled to arbitrary mediator masses.

hep-ph.title: Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at FCC-ee
hep-ph.author: Dario Buttazzo, Gabriele Levati, Yang Ma, Fabio Maltoni, Paride Paradisi, ZeQiang Wang
hep-ph.abstract: We study the sensitivity of future high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $\tau$ lepton within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We analyse several complementary processes across the FCC-ee operating stages and show that the exceptional luminosity and clean environment of future $e^+e^-$ colliders allow for substantial improvements over current limits from LEP and the LHC. The $e^+e^- \to \tau^+\tau^-$ process provides excellent sensitivity to weak dipole operators through resonant $Z$ production and $Z$-pole energy scans, while $\gamma\gamma \to \tau^+\tau^-$ yields the strongest constraint on the anomalous magnetic moment owing to the dominance of linear interference effects in the near-threshold region. Higher-energy stages improve the sensitivity to the $\tau$ electric dipole moment. The radiative processes $e^+e^- \to \tau^+\tau^-\gamma$ and $H\to\tau^+\tau^-\gamma$ provide complementary, though subleading, probes of $\tau$ dipole operators. Combining all channels, we estimate the statistical reach at the 95% CL to be $|\Delta a_\tau|<2.8\times10^{-5}$, $|d_\tau|<2.5\times10^{-18}\,e\,{\rm cm}$, $|\Delta a_\tau^Z|<1.0\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_\tau^Z|<4.4\times10^{-19}\,e\,{\rm cm}$, improving upon the current bounds by several orders of magnitude. These projections quantify the potential statistical reach of the FCC-ee program, motivating dedicated studies incorporating detector effects, systematic uncertainties, and higher-order theoretical predictions.

hep-ph.title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
hep-ph.author: Abdias Aires, Tatsuya Daniel
hep-ph.abstract: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a magnetic spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal has a maximum at $2k_c$ and, as expected from momentum conservation, has a sharp cutoff at that scale. We apply this analysis to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160$ MeV the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-10 MeV on such viable models.

hep-ph.title: Evidence for Kaluza-Klein excitations of the graviton, gluon and quark at LHC
hep-ph.author: Alain Le Yaouanc, François Richard
hep-ph.abstract: Following our paper showing evidence for a tower of Kaluza-Klein gravitons, we interpret the massive 4 jet excesses observed by CMS. They could come from the decay of two heavy KK gluons gkk(3.6TeV) and gkk(8.6TeV) into pairs of KK quarks qkk(1TeV) and qkk(2.1TeV). Present limits on gkk into top pairs seem to exclude gkk(3.6TeV) but these limits assume a dominant decay into top pairs, which can be questioned as was the case in our study of KK graviton decays. The cross section predicted for gkk(8.6) requires a BR into a pair of qkk(2.1TeV) or order 10% which is not unlikely. We also discuss the issue of a hierarchy between the KK graviton masses and the vector boson masses and the solution provided by the RS multi-brane models. Prospects for reaching a 6 s.d. level local evidence with RUN3 data are promising for 3 channels. KK excitations of the Z boson are discussed and appear also promising. Indirect evidences for these particles are also presented.

hep-ph.title: Searches for new particle physics by methods of classical and neutrino astronomy
hep-ph.author: Sergey Troitsky
hep-ph.abstract: Selected astrophysical methods for testing particle-physics models are reviewed. Stellar structure and evolution constrain additional channels of energy loss and transport; high-energy photon propagation probes photon mixing with new particles and modifications of electron-positron pair production; large-volume neutrino telescopes are used to search for magnetic monopoles, neutrinos from superheavy dark-matter decay, and non-standard neutrino propagation. Recent applications of these methods are discussed, involving the tip of the red-giant branch in the color-luminosity diagram, gamma-ray burst 221009A, and data from the Baikal Gigaton Volume Detector (Baikal-GVD) and the IceCube experiment. In each case, particle-physics parameters are inferred through a forward model that accounts for the response to new physics, propagation, detection, and nuisance parameters.

hep-ph.title: An interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles
hep-ph.author: Zhi-zhong Xing
hep-ph.abstract: We conjecture a novel interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles: $\theta^{}_{23} = \left(\theta^{}_{12} + \theta^{}_{13}\right)/2 + \pi/8$, which predicts $\theta^{}_{23} = 43.46^\circ \pm 0.26^\circ$ with inputs of the latest JUNO and Daya Bay precision data. A simple ansatz is proposed to derive this phenomenologically favored and experimentally testable angle relation, and a new expansion of the lepton flavor mixing matrix in powers of a single small parameter is presented as a by-product.

hep-ph.title: Strongly supercooled first-order phase transitions: monopole abundance, entropy production and homogeneity consistency
hep-ph.author: Chen Zhang, Yue Niu, Xin Zhang
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate whether monopole production in the early universe from a first-order phase transition in a unified gauge theory can be significantly suppressed if the phase transition is subject to strong supercooling but still completes successfully. This is facilitated by adopting a Gaussian nucleation model and assuming the false vacuum energy released is transferred to sectors which behave effectively as radiation in terms of cosmological evolution. We distinguish three criteria of phase-transition completion: the comoving measure completion (CMC) characterized by the eventual vanishing of the false-vacuum fraction (FVF), the physical volume completion (PVC) characterized by the eventual vanishing of the physical volume of false vacuum, and the asymptotic thermodynamic completion (ATC), which refers to the finiteness of total entropy production. Assuming an idealized Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) cosmology, it is shown that the three criteria share exactly the same completion boundary, away from which they are completely equivalent. It is further shown that monopole abundance can be arbitrarily suppressed for parameter points approaching the completion boundary from the successful side. Nevertheless, for parameter points too close to the completion boundary, justification of the self-consistency of a homogeneous FLRW cosmology is difficult. We propose the use of the Hubble-scale FVF root-mean-square fluctuation to diagnose the homogeneity consistency issue, and find that arbitrarily strong suppression of monopole abundance relative to a reasonable Kibble estimate is not justifiable in terms of homogeneity consistency. These findings also have implications for gravitational wave production in strongly supercooled phase transitions.

hep-ph.title: Dark Matter-Dark Radiation Interactions and the Hubble Tension
hep-ph.author: Manuel A. Buen-Abad, Zackaria Chacko, Ina Flood, Can Kilic, Gustavo Marques-Tavares, Taewook Youn
hep-ph.abstract: Models in which a subcomponent of dark matter interacts with dark radiation have been proposed as a solution to the Hubble tension. In this framework, the interacting subcomponent of dark matter is in thermal equilibrium with the dark radiation in the early universe, but decouples from it around the time of matter-radiation equality. We study this general class of models and evaluate the quality of fit to recent cosmological data on the cosmic microwave background (from Planck 2018 and ACT DR6), baryon acoustic oscillations, large-scale structure, supernovae type Ia, and Cepheid variables. We focus on three benchmark scenarios that differ in the rate at which the dark matter decouples from the dark radiation, resulting in different patterns of dark acoustic oscillations. Fitting without ACT DR6 data, we find that all three scenarios significantly reduce the Hubble tension relative to $\Lambda$CDM, with an exponentially fast decoupling being the most preferred. The tension is reduced to less than $2 \, \sigma$ in fits that don't include the SH0ES collaboration results as part of the data and to less than $1 \, \sigma$ when these are included. The preference for the interacting model is substantially reduced when ACT DR6 data are included. We find that the largest $H_0$ value at the $95 \%$ confidence region is $70.1$ km/s/Mpc without the SH0ES data, leading to only a mild reduction in the tension. This increases to $72.5$ km/s/Mpc, corresponding to a reduction in the tension to less than $3 \, \sigma$, if the SH0ES results are included in the fit.

hep-ph.title: Lattice QCD study of the $K^*(892)$ resonance at the physical point
hep-ph.author: Qu-Zhi Li, Chuan Liu, Liuming Liu, Peng Sun, Jia-Jun Wu, Zhiguang Xiao, Yi-Bo Yang, Han-Qing Zheng
hep-ph.abstract: We present a lattice QCD study of the $K^*(892)$ resonance using eight $N_f=2+1$ Wilson-Clover ensembles with three lattice spacings and six pion masses ranging from 135 to 320 MeV. For each ensemble, a large number of finite volume energy levels in the $P$-wave $K\pi$ channel are determined. The energy dependence of the scattering phase shift is then obtained from Lüscher's finite-volume method. To systematically assess parametrization dependence, the amplitude is described using three different models, which yield consistent results. The resulting phase shifts show a clear resonant behavior for all ensembles, and the corresponding $K^*(892)$ resonance pole is identified on the second Riemann sheet in the complex energy plane. The pole positions are extrapolated to the physical pion mass and the continuum limit, yielding a $K^*(892)$ resonance located at $\sqrt{s_0} = [882.10\binom{+7.36}{-10.29} (0.30) -i22.73(3.32)(0.63)] \mathrm{MeV}$, which is in excellent agreement with the experimental value. The quoted uncertainty includes the statistical uncertainty and systematic uncertainties associated with the choice of fit windows and three parameterizations of the scattering amplitude.

hep-ph.title: Quantum-information diagnostics of cosmological perturbations with nontrivial sound speed in inflation
hep-ph.author: Shi-Cheng Liu, Lei-Hua Liu, Bichu Li, Hai-Qing Zhang, Peng-Zhang He
hep-ph.abstract: In this work, we systematically investigate the quantum-information diagnostics of cosmological perturbations with a nontrivial sound speed, utilizing a normalized open two-mode squeezed-state framework. Rather than introducing new observables, our analysis focuses on how a modified sound speed dynamically reshapes the Schrödinger evolution of the squeezing parameters ($r_k$ and $\phi_k$). We demonstrate how these dynamical changes are inherited by the reduced density matrix of the observable sector. By employing a sound-speed-resonance parametrization, we derive and evaluate the purity, von Neumann entropy, Rényi entropies, and logarithmic negativity. We introduce a bounded variable $x = \tanh r_k$ and perform numerical simulations within the inflationary regime. Our numerical results reveal that a nontrivial sound speed significantly suppresses the purity of the reduced state, indicating enhanced effective mixedness. Simultaneously, it strongly amplifies and modulates both the entropic and entanglement diagnostics. More precisely, a nontrivial sound speed postpones the onset of classicality by modulating the decoherence process. Ultimately, we show that a nontrivial sound speed leaves distinct and identifiable quantum-information signatures within the entanglement structure of the early universe.

hep-ph.title: Assessing the enrichment of heat-producing elements in deep-mantle structures using a directional geoneutrino detector
hep-ph.author: Zhihao Xu, Misaki Hosoya, William F. McDonough, Taichi Sakai, Hiroko Watanabe
hep-ph.abstract: Determining the spatial distribution of heat-producing elements (HPEs) within the Earth is critical for understanding the planet's thermal and chemical evolution. A central debate is whether domains in the deep mantle, particularly the Large Low-Velocity Provinces (LLVP), represent anomalous, radiogenically enriched reservoirs. Variation in the surface flux of geoneutrinos provide a direct probe of Earth's internal radioactivity. However, current continental located detectors measure only the angle-integrated flux, leading to strong spatial trade-offs that substantially limit the ability of practical networks to uniquely resolve mantle compositional heterogeneity. In this study, we quantify the potential of directional geoneutrino detection to overcome this limitation. By evaluating realistic LLVP geometries in the context of the proposed Ocean Bottom Detector (OBD), we demonstrate that resolving the incoming direction of geoneutrinos can substantially improve the precision with which HPE enrichment in LLVPs can be constrained relative to the surrounding mantle, for a range of target angular resolutions envisioned for a future directional geoneutrino detector. These results indicate that future directional geoneutrino measurements could help determine whether LLVP host enhanced HPE abundances and assess their contribution to Earth's radiogenic heat budget. Such measurements would provide a new observational constraint on the chemical heterogeneity of the deep mantle and its role in Earth's long-term thermal evolution.

hep-ph.title: Particle accelerators as a path to intergovernmental collaboration: the case of the first electron positron collider and the power of theoretical physics
hep-ph.author: Giulia Pancheri
hep-ph.abstract: I revisit the history of the first matter-antimatter collider built in Italy in 1960 and carried to success through an inter-European collaboration with France, to underline the need for large intergovernmental efforts in the realization of particle accelerators such as the proposed electron synchrotron in the Greater Caribbean region. The foundational role of the Austrian born theoretical physicist Bruno Touschek and his life path through Europe before and after World War II is briefly recalled. The role of CERN as a post-war intergovernmental institution in jump-starting the international collaboration between the Frascati National Laboratories in Italy and the Laboratoire de l'Accelerateur Lineaire d'Orsay in France is highlighted through historical documents, and contributions from interviews with the protagonists of Touschek's game-changing proposal.

hep-ph.title: Accelerating systems as probes of Lorentz violation
hep-ph.author: Quentin G. Bailey, Nils A. Nilsson, Sawyer J. Star
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the Fulling-Davies-Unruh effect in a local Lorentz-violating effective field theory, focusing on the quantum-field response of accelerated detectors. We canonically quantize a real scalar field exactly in the coefficients for Lorentz violation. The dispersion relation, Hamiltonian, and massless and massive Wightman functions are obtained. We determine the conditions under which the scalar dynamics preserves boost symmetry and distinguish these from the weaker conditions required for stationarity along a single accelerated worldline. The Wightman functions are used to construct the finite-time Unruh-DeWitt response for a uniformly accelerated detector. For generic coefficients the response is nonstationary and depends on both the duration and temporal location of the measurement. The spectrum, which is the resulting excitation rate as a function of the energy level difference in the detector, is obtained numerically. It shows discernable differences with the usual massive thermal spectrum for dimensionless coefficients on the order of $10^{-7}$. Experimental implications of the result are discussed. As an alternative viewpoint, we place Lorentz violation in the point-particle sector, derive the exact trajectory generated by a constant electric field, and study the proper-time Fourier response of a conventional scalar wave along the modified trajectory.

hep-ph.title: Probing Dark Matter via the Migdal Effect in LUX-ZEPLIN Data
hep-ph.author: Yang Yu, Lei Feng
hep-ph.abstract: Sub-GeV dark matter (DM) particles deposit little energy in conventional direct-detection experiments and are therefore difficult to probe, but the Migdal effect provides an electronic signal from atomic ionization accompanying the recoil. Using the new results of the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment with a 4.2 tonne-year exposure, we evaluate the sensitivity of the Migdal effect to the spin-independent DM--nucleon scattering cross section. For masses between $350~\mathrm{MeV}$ and $10~\mathrm{GeV}$, the projected 90\% upper limits range from $6.5\times10^{-37}$ to $3.1\times10^{-43}~\mathrm{cm^2}$. These limits are then used to constrain the minimal scalar- and vector-mediator DM models. For the light-mediator DM model, the constraint on the coupling reaches $\alpha\simeq 10^{-12}$, which is stronger than or comparable to the constraints from kaon decays, stellar cooling, and SN1987A.

hep-ph.title: Strangeness in the Chiral Mean Field model phase diagram
hep-ph.author: Mateus Reinke Pelicer, Nikolas Cruz-Camacho, Rajesh Kumar, Veronica Dexheimer, Jacquelyn Noronha-Hostler
hep-ph.abstract: We explore the phase diagram of the Chiral Mean Field model in the space of temperature and baryon, charge, and strangeness chemical potentials, focusing on the role of the strangeness direction. At low density, a negative $\mu_S$ leads to finite strangeness in the nuclear liquid--gas transition and rotates the order parameter away from the purely baryonic direction. The critical mode remains baryon dominated over the $\mu_S$ range considered, while the critical locus develops a strong parametrization dependence once multistrange baryons appear. At higher density, a separate first-order transition toward strangeness-rich hadronic matter appears only for one of the two parametrizations considered, emphasizing its interaction dependence. The high density transition reorganizes octet-dominated matter into decuplet-dominated matter: $\Delta$ baryons provide most of the baryon-density discontinuity, while $\Xi^*(1530)$ baryons provide the largest contribution to the strangeness-density discontinuity. Its order parameter is dominated by the strangeness density, and its normalized direction in the $BQS$ space changes little with temperature even as the discontinuity vanishes at the critical point. The critical baryon chemical potential changes by almost $1$~GeV over $\mu_S\in [-300, 300]$~MeV. We characterize both transitions using the fixed-temperature $BQS$ susceptibility matrix, the density discontinuity between the coexisting phases, and a generalized Clausius--Clapeyron relation. This work also accompanies the release of \cmfpp{} \texttt{v2.0.0} as part of the MUSES framework. The extension of the initial release includes, among other features, finite-temperature thermodynamics, new interactions and parametrizations, and susceptibility calculations based on a Jacobian method.

hep-ph.title: Spatiotemporal K-Shape: Reconstructing inhomogeneous condensate profiles on the lattice
hep-ph.author: Keita Horie, Rin Kagami, Chiho Nonaka
hep-ph.abstract: Spatially modulated chiral condensates can affect the phase structure of dense QCD effective models. Understanding such order requires characterizing its real-space structure as well as detecting a modulation. Spatial two-point correlators retain the ensemble-averaged power spectrum but discard relative Fourier phases, leaving the configuration shapes undetermined in general. We propose the Spatiotemporal K-Shape method to extract representative shapes from lattice Monte Carlo ensembles without assuming a functional form. The method extends K-Shape clustering to periodic lattice fields, aligning configurations modulo translations and, optionally, a global sign or phase before extracting cluster centroids. Comparisons across clusterings assess whether one representative shape suffices. Controlled tests recover distinct profiles with identical correlators and separate mixtures of different shapes. Applied to the $(1+1)$-dimensional Gross-Neveu model with $N_f=8$, the method extracts non-sinusoidal profiles with two sign changes at two chemical potentials and separates multiple shape families at a third, where a single centroid is insufficient. Including the discrete chiral sign symmetry in the alignment can fold domain-length fluctuations into an asymmetric centroid without implying a preferred ensemble asymmetry. The method thus complements correlator diagnostics with representative real-space shapes and information on their diversity. The application to the Gross-Neveu model provides a testing ground for configuration-based studies of inhomogeneous order relevant to the QCD phase diagram.

hep-lat.title: Generative diffusion models for lattice field theory
hep-lat.author: Gert Aarts, Diaa E. Habibi, Lingxiao Wang, Kai Zhou
hep-lat.abstract: Generative diffusion models offer a new route to ensemble generation in lattice field theory. The backward, or denoising, process underlying these models is a stochastic process with a learned, time-dependent drift, which leads to a clear connection with stochastic quantisation. After reviewing this correspondence, I turn to theories with a sign problem. There the complex Boltzmann weight obstructs direct sampling, but complex Langevin dynamics can sometimes evade the sign problem by generating configurations on a complexified manifold, distributed according to a real and semi-positive distribution. This distribution is not known in closed form. I discuss how this distribution can be learned from complex Langevin data using score-based and, in particular, energy-based diffusion models. The latter give direct access to the unnormalised distribution itself, which can subsequently be used as the weight in a standard Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation. Results are shown for a simple quartic model with a complex action.

hep-lat.title: Positivity, Noise, and Cones
hep-lat.author: Ryan Abbott, Claire X. Davis, Sarah Fields, William I. Jay, Patrick Oare, Matteo Saccardi
hep-lat.abstract: As a consequence of causality, Euclidean-time correlation functions in quantum field theory are subject to constraints in the form of positivity conditions on certain Hankel matrices. Such conditions define convex conic structures. Correlation functions computed numerically using Monte Carlo techniques generally contain statistical fluctuations that violate the positivity conditions. This work describes a projection procedure, based on the convex conic geometry induced by the positivity conditions and a statistical covariance matrix, that can be used to restore positivity, providing a unique decomposition for noisy correlators into causal and acausal components. In contrast to previous literature, this work explicitly leverages the conic structure and not just the convex nature of the causal space. The projection can be computed using primal-dual interior-point methods. Constrained projection gives rise to observable-specific frequentist confidence intervals for smeared spectral densities in the causal bootstrap of [Phys. Rev. D 114, 074510 (2026)]. Analytic results are supported with numerical examples.

hep-lat.title: Interpretable uncertainties for bounds on spectral functionals from Euclidean correlators
hep-lat.author: Christoph Lehner
hep-lat.abstract: Positivity of the spectral density, combined with a $\chi^2$ measure of compatibility with the data, bounds every linear functional of the spectral density of a Euclidean correlator to an interval. We show how such an interval is turned into a central value with statistical and systematic errors that have a definite meaning. We first show that, at typical precision, the best positive fit of noisy data has $\chi^2_{\min}>0$, with a probability bounded from below by the distance of the noise-free data from the boundary of the set of data of positive spectra. Numerically, it does not depend on the number of states. The threshold must therefore be set relative to $\chi^2_{\min}$. With $\Delta\chi^2=1$, the interval reproduces Gaussian error propagation when positivity does not act, and positivity can only narrow it. We define the statistical error by the jackknife and the systematic error as the remaining, non-Gaussian part of the interval, which becomes a systematic error that does not decrease with the statistics in the high-statistics limit. Coverage tests for correlators and for smeared spectral densities and step functions give nominal coverage for outputs determined by the data and mostly conservative coverage otherwise. The exceptions are effects of the statistical error on the error estimate that disappear as the statistics is increased. Additional bounds on the spectral density, for example from perturbation theory, further reduce the systematic error substantially without loss of coverage. For long-distance correlators the method uses the same information as the bounding method, and its error agrees with that of the bounding method up to the remaining gap between the bounds.

hep-lat.title: Light fermions can trigger a Brout-Englert-Higgs effect
hep-lat.author: Axel Maas, Sofie Martins, Georg Wieland
hep-lat.abstract: The Brout-Englert-Higgs effect produces the masses of the Standard Model particles. However, the cause of this effect is unknown. Beyond-the-Standard-Model theories aim to find the source of this effect, for example using a composite Higgs and dynamically generating its vacuum expectation value. In this paper, we show evidence from lattice simulations with vectorially coupled fermions and without Yukawa couplings that the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect could be triggered by the light masses of fermions. This suggests that an explanation entirely within the Standard Model could be possible. Moreover, our results are consistent with weak couplings and fermions can only impact the Higgs potential at NNLO. This implies a so far unidentified mechanism in an SU(2) scalar-fermion-gauge system that produces a non-zero vacuum expectation value. In addition, we find that the transition from a QCD-like behavior to a Higgs-like behavior happens when the fermion mass falls below twice the W/Z mass: a threshold that is integer valued but not connected to other critical physical behavior.

hep-lat.title: Perspective on Proton Transversity Distribution Functions
hep-lat.author: Ke-Xin Zeng, Peng Cheng, Yang Yu, Daniele Binosi, Craig D. Roberts
hep-lat.abstract: Using available information on proton tensor charges and constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD), Ansaetze are introduced for hadron-scale in-proton valence-quark transversity distributions functions (DFs). The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $\zeta_{2} = 2\,$GeV. Although the approach is largely algebraic, its predictions remain viable after comparisons with results obtained using computationally intensive methods. Thus, given the scarcity of data that can today be used for inference of proton transversity DFs, it may be worth using the results herein to inform and constrain related experiments and phenomenological fits.

hep-lat.title: Topological signatures of criticality: the Ising case
hep-lat.author: Tak-Shing Chan, Paweł Dłotko, Jacek Gulgowski, Biagio Lucini, Mateusz Masłowski, Davide Vadacchino
hep-lat.abstract: Topological properties of microscopic configurations may provide additional insight into phase transitions beyond conventional thermodynamic observables. We investigate this idea in the two-dimensional Ising model on square and triangular lattices by associating cell complexes with the positive and negative spin domains and constructing an Euler-characteristic observable from their difference. We provide the expression relating this quantity to conventional observables of the Ising model. This derivation allows us to understand its expected behavior physically. As a byproduct, we show that at any finite positive temperature the expectation of the Euler characteristic exceeds a positive, lattice-size-independent bound, hence disproving a previously suggested conjecture. Monte Carlo simulations combined with multihistogram reweighting show that this spin-odd topological observable exhibits order-parameter-like behavior near the ferromagnetic transition. Finite-size scaling of its susceptibility yields pseudocritical temperatures that converge to the known critical temperature for both lattice geometries. On the square lattice, the leading-order estimate of the critical exponent obtained from the topological observable depends more strongly on the fitting range than the magnetization estimate. This behavior is consistent with stronger subleading finite-size corrections, as supported by fits including an additional correction term. On the triangular lattice, the corresponding estimate remains consistent with the theoretical Ising value. Our study suggests that topologically defined quantities such as the Euler characteristic can provide an alternative way to locate order-disorder phase transitions in the systems considered here. Since the definition of these observables is purely geometrical, they can provide useful insights in cases in which order parameters cannot be constructed.

hep-lat.title: Total Angular Momentum Assignments in the Hadron Spectrum
hep-lat.author: TheHADLENS Collaboration:S. Rostami, Omid Zamani Jamshidi, B.Dehghanzad, K. Azizi
hep-lat.abstract: Predicting the total angular momentum $J$ for hadronic resonances whose spins have not yet been experimentally determined constitutes an important step in the spectroscopy of observed hadrons. In the present study, we develop a data-driven model in order to predict the value of $ J $ for hadrons with unknown spins using a dataset of known mesons and baryons from the PDG, including information on their quark content, isospin, parity, mass and other spectroscopic features. In particular, we employ XGBoost classifiers along with nested optimization in order to discover spectroscopic patterns across different hadronic sectors. We also prepare a systematic list of hadrons with unknown or poorly determined values of $ J $, and study spin-parity assignments for those hadrons. Since the parity hypothesis is taken as an input to the model, our model predicts the value of $ J $ conditional on a given parity hypothesis rather than independently determining the full $J^P$ assignment. Our predictions for several theoretically studied states show good agreement with results from quark models, QCD sum rules, molecular models, and other phenomenological approaches, while predictions for some other states differ from existing theoretical assignments. These differences motivate further theoretical investigations and may be tested by future experimental measurements.

hep-lat.title: Radii of Sn Isotopes near the Proton Dripline from Nuclear Lattice Effective Field Theory
hep-lat.author: Fabian Hildenbrand, Serdar Elhatisari, Ulf-G. Meißner
hep-lat.abstract: We present the first $\textit{ab initio}$ lattice calculations of charge and matter radii of tin isotopes $^{96}$Sn, $^{98}$Sn, $^{100}$Sn, $^{102}$Sn and $^{104}$Sn near the proton dripline using nuclear lattice effective field theory with high-fidelity two- and three-nucleon forces combined with the partial-pinhole algorithm. The resulting radii are larger then predicted from other ab-initio methods. We find that variations of the three-nucleon interaction reveal substantial radius differences even among interactions with similar binding energies. We intensively discuss of the role of different choices of the three-body forces.

hep-lat.title: Lattice QCD study of the $K^*(892)$ resonance at the physical point
hep-lat.author: Qu-Zhi Li, Chuan Liu, Liuming Liu, Peng Sun, Jia-Jun Wu, Zhiguang Xiao, Yi-Bo Yang, Han-Qing Zheng
hep-lat.abstract: We present a lattice QCD study of the $K^*(892)$ resonance using eight $N_f=2+1$ Wilson-Clover ensembles with three lattice spacings and six pion masses ranging from 135 to 320 MeV. For each ensemble, a large number of finite volume energy levels in the $P$-wave $K\pi$ channel are determined. The energy dependence of the scattering phase shift is then obtained from Lüscher's finite-volume method. To systematically assess parametrization dependence, the amplitude is described using three different models, which yield consistent results. The resulting phase shifts show a clear resonant behavior for all ensembles, and the corresponding $K^*(892)$ resonance pole is identified on the second Riemann sheet in the complex energy plane. The pole positions are extrapolated to the physical pion mass and the continuum limit, yielding a $K^*(892)$ resonance located at $\sqrt{s_0} = [882.10\binom{+7.36}{-10.29} (0.30) -i22.73(3.32)(0.63)] \mathrm{MeV}$, which is in excellent agreement with the experimental value. The quoted uncertainty includes the statistical uncertainty and systematic uncertainties associated with the choice of fit windows and three parameterizations of the scattering amplitude.

hep-lat.title: Finite-Volume Step Scaling at Fixed Truncation in (2+1)D Hamiltonian U(1) Lattice Gauge Theory
hep-lat.author: Alessio Negro, Emil Otis Rosanowski, Lena Funcke, Timo Jakobs, Karl Jansen, Paul Ludwig, Carsten Urbach
hep-lat.abstract: We propose a finite-volume scheme to perform controlled continuum extrapolations of the lattice step-scaling function, a key ingredient for determining the running coupling in a Hamiltonian lattice gauge theory in small volumes. As a testbed, we employ a dual Hamiltonian formulation of pure U(1) gauge theory in (2+1) dimensions and an operator basis that remains efficient toward weak coupling. We describe the implementation of static external charges on the spatial lattice and study, using matrix product states, the resulting confining string, from which we extract the static potential and a force-based renormalized coupling. The result is a stable lattice-spacing extrapolation at fixed truncation $\Lambda$ and transverse lattice extent $N_y$; a full compact-U(1) continuum result additionally requires $\Lambda$ convergence and control of the transverse physical extent. The method is readily extendable to other gauge groups and dimensions, providing a pathway toward Hamiltonian step-scaling studies in other theories.

hep-lat.title: Spatiotemporal K-Shape: Reconstructing inhomogeneous condensate profiles on the lattice
hep-lat.author: Keita Horie, Rin Kagami, Chiho Nonaka

hep-lat.title: Transverse-momentum resummation effects on angular coefficients in Z and W boson hadroproduction
hep-lat.author: Stefano Camarda, Giancarlo Ferrera, Lorenzo Rossi, Gabriele Francesco Sala
hep-lat.abstract: We present a comprehensive analysis of the angular coefficients of $Z$ and $W$ boson production at hadron colliders in different kinematical ranges, using data from the ATLAS, LHCb, and CMS Collaborations at the LHC, including the recent CMS measurement at $\sqrt{s}=13$~TeV, as well as CDF data at the Tevatron. We provide theoretical predictions obtained by consistently combining the resummation of logarithmically enhanced QCD corrections at small transverse momentum $q_T$ up to next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy (NNLL) with the fixed-order calculation through $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_S^2)$. The fixed-order helicity cross sections entering the finite component are evaluated using the new complete analytic NLO calculation implemented in the DYTurbo program. This implementation makes it possible to obtain fast and numerically stable predictions for all the angular coefficients and to perform an extensive study of their theoretical uncertainties. We quantify the impact of transverse-momentum resummation on the angular coefficients and we estimate the associated theoretical uncertainties, including scale variations, parton distribution functions, non-perturbative effects, the treatment of the transition region and the recoil prescription used to generate the lepton angular distribution of the resummed component. Within the estimated theoretical uncertainties, resummation improves the description of several measurements, particularly for $A_2$, while its impact on $A_0$ depends more strongly on the dataset and on the theoretical choices. The Lam--Tung combination $A_0-A_2$ is essentially unaffected by resummation.

hep-th.title: Commuting integrals of motion for free bosonic CFTs revisited: certified densities, spectral rigidity, and an exact identification at the c=1 branch point
hep-th.author: Evgueniy Vitchev
hep-th.abstract: We revisit the commuting local integrals of motion for free bosonic CFTs constructed inhep-th/0404195as input data for integrable boundary states, using exact-arithmetic operator-product engines. A bootstrap lemma reduces its overdetermined bilinear commutativity systems to a distinguished odd charge D plus linear kernel problems -- conditionally on even-spin vacancy, a machine-verified but finite-range input. For the Z_2 x Z_2 "paperclip" family we publish the spin-7 density P_8, prove [I_3,I_5]=[I_3,I_7]=[I_5,I_7]=0 identically in n, and verify the Lukyanov-Vitchev-Zamolodchikov four-screening characterization at spins 7 and 9 at sampled n. For the A_2^(2) family we give an exact Coulomb-gas dictionary to the dual Phi_{1,2}/Phi_{2,1} perturbations (that identification itself being classical, Zamolodchikov; Smirnov), whence the infinite hierarchy at all spins 6n+-1 follows by the Feigin-Frenkel affine-Toda theorem; our contribution is the certified dictionary, not a new all-spin construction. At c=1 the tower's defining charges are exactly quantum KdV at c_{1,4}=-25/2 -- the all-odd sector of the Freeman-Hornfeck-West family: the hierarchy embeds at every odd spin, equality verified through spin 15, all-spin multiplicity one open. We exclude or disfavor the named non-KdV candidates at the tested loci and identify the self-dual degeneracy as L(1,0). Through spin 11, the generic centralizer of I_3 is, for all three Z_2 x O(N) "cylindrical" families, one-dimensional at odd and zero at even spins, with Q(t)-symbolic charges at spins 7, 9, 11 and an explained fiber jump at N=-2. We certify the published 2004 low-spin formulas and record five corrections (one presumed). All-spin statements are made only where proved, finite-range otherwise. We close with a corank-character conjecture linking the rank deficiencies of the bilinear systems to characters of screening kernels.

hep-th.title: Exact Solutions to Matrix Models and String Theories: The Global Construction
hep-th.author: Jasper Kager, João Rodrigues, Ricardo Schiappa, Maximilian Schwick, Noam Tamarin
hep-th.abstract: Exact nonperturbative solutions to matrix models and string theories are obtained in closed-form via a discrete-Fourier/Zak-transform representation of their partition-function resurgent-transseries. Examples include all hermitian one-matrix models (paired with their topological string duals) alongside all their multicritical and minimal-string double-scaling limits. The resulting structure is resonant, necessarily including both eigenvalues (D-branes) and anti-eigenvalues (negative-tension-branes). In a complementary preceding paper these solutions were extensively verified at the local level. In order to study them globally across their phase diagrams, complete non-linear Stokes data (and corresponding connection formulae) are still needed -- all of which are obtained herein. This involves a careful study of (anti-) eigenvalue tunneling across the complete multi-sheeted structure of their associated spectral-curves, and how the result descends from multi-cut smooth-curves to single-cut singular-curves -- all of which are extensively checked via large-order analysis and matrix-integral computations. Making use of the resulting exact Stokes automorphisms, nonperturbative solutions can be fully tested, from weak-to-strong 't Hooft coupling, as well as from large-to-small N, and for any complex-values of all parameters, by correctly implementing Stokes-transitions at the crossing of all possible Stokes-lines. Several analytical and numerical tests are carried through in diverse examples covering from matrix models through non-critical strings, which produce very sharp numerical matches fully validating our exact analytical expressions. Anti-eigenvalues or negative-tension D-branes are an absolutely essential part of the story in order to find such precise agreements.

hep-th.title: Localizing the M-Theory Path Integral: Membrane Instantons
hep-th.author: Pietro Benetti Genolini, Jerome P. Gauntlett, Jaeha Park, James Sparks
hep-th.abstract: We propose a formula for M2-instanton contributions to the M-theory path integral, incorporating quantum corrections to all orders in the Planck length. The M2-brane action is determined by relative equivariant localization, while an equivariant Dolbeault character computes the one-loop determinant. Continuous families of M2-branes are treated by equivariant localization on their moduli spaces. For M-theory backgrounds dual to ABJM theory, we compute single instanton contributions from linear holomorphic fillings to the sphere partition function and the topologically twisted index associated with supersymmetric $AdS_4$ black holes. Our results reproduce known field theory instanton coefficients and give new analytic predictions for mass and squashing deformations at all Chern-Simons levels. For the $V^{5,2}$ theory, we compute new instanton contributions and establish an exact relation between its partition function at special squashing and that of ABJM theory on the round three-sphere.

hep-th.title: A Positive Metric on Four-Dimensional QFTs
hep-th.author: Thomas Hartman, Grégoire Mathys, Andreas Stergiou
hep-th.abstract: A natural metric on the space of four-dimensional quantum field theories was introduced by Jack and Osborn in classic work on the local renormalization group. In perturbation theory, the Jack-Osborn metric determines the flow of the $a$-anomaly, and positivity implies the $a$-theorem. We derive a non-perturbative generalization of the Jack-Osborn metric and show that it is non-negative by the averaged null energy condition (ANEC). Consequently, the ANEC implies the strong $a$-theorem, and provides the monotonic function along the flow. The method is based on spectral analysis of the three-point function $\langle \mathcal{O}_I \mathcal{E} \mathcal{O}_J\rangle$, where the $\mathcal{O}_I$ are relevant operators and $\mathcal{E}$ is the averaged null energy. This three-point function is decomposed under the spectrum of null rotations that fix the light ray, leading to a positivity condition at each impact parameter.

hep-th.title: Horizon kinematics and the fine structure induced by finite-energy Hawking radiation
hep-th.author: M. A. Aguirre Cortés, Moisés Bravo-Gaete, Julio A. Méndez-Zavaleta, Efraín Rojas Marcial
hep-th.abstract: Hawking radiation can modify the horizon structure of a black hole through the loss of mass and global charges. Investigating this process through quantum tunneling, we develop a systematic strategy to reconstruct horizon displacements under finite-energy emission, even when their radii are not explicitly known. Inversion of the horizon condition allows to follow roots's displacements along sequences of static geometries.
